The test image shows a tomato leaf with:
- Scattered small yellow/pale dots across the surface
- General chlorosis/yellowing
- Largely green tissue remaining between spots
- Some edge browning

Top candidates: Powdery Mildew, Leaf Mold, Bacterial Speck, Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus. Let me view one reference from each.

**Analysis of test image:**
- Tomato leaf with scattered small pale/yellowish dots across the surface
- Leaf remains mostly green
- Some edge browning and slight chlorosis

**Reference comparison:**
- **Powdery Mildew** (CDDM_116): Shows distinct discrete white powdery circular patches — the test image has smaller, more numerous scattered dots, less consistent
- **Leaf Mold** (CDDM_313): Shows pale blotchy chlorotic spots on leaf surface — closer in character to the scattered pale dots in the test image
- **Bacterial Speck** (Bugwood_14): Dark/black spots with yellow halos — clearly not matching
- **TSWV** (Bugwood_3): Whole-plant wilting and dark bronzing — not matching

The scattered small pale/yellowish dots across an otherwise green tomato leaf most closely match Leaf Mold (Fulvia fulva), which causes yellow chlorotic spots on the upper leaf surface. The dots are more dispersed and numerous than the distinct powdery patches of Powdery Mildew.
